content.user_title: Analyze Health Notes With Claude Ally Health
content.value_statement: Health notes and symptoms can be hard to organize for AI review. This skill structures wellness questions for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Provides a concise health assistant overview for AI conversations.
Guides medical information analysis at a general information level.
Supports symptom tracking prompts and wellness guidance discussions.
Defines when to use the skill for health assistant workflows.
Links to the public source repository for additional context.
limitations: Does not provide diagnosis, treatment decisions, or emergency medical instructions.
Does not include executable tools, data storage, or automated health integrations.
Does not validate medical facts against clinical guidelines.
Contains only broad guidance in a short SKILL.md file.

use_cases.title: Organize personal symptoms
use_cases.description: A patient or caregiver can summarize recurring symptoms before a non-urgent appointment.

use_cases.title: Review wellness notes
use_cases.description: A wellness coach can structure general wellness observations without presenting them as medical advice.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a health prompt skill
use_cases.description: A marketplace reviewer can understand the intended health assistant behavior and visible safety boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize My Health Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Claude Ally Health to organize these health notes. Separate symptoms, timing, questions, and items to discuss with a clinician.

prompt_templates.title: Track Symptom Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Claude Ally Health to compare these symptom entries. Identify repeated patterns, missing details, and neutral follow-up questions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Wellness Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Claude Ally Health to draft general wellness guidance from these notes. Avoid diagnosis and separate evidence from assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Health Assistant Response
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Claude Ally Health to review this draft response. Flag medical overclaims, unclear safety language, and missing clinician referral points.

output_examples.input: I have three weeks of sleep notes and headaches.
output: The response groups symptoms by date and frequency.
It lists missing details such as severity, duration, and triggers.
It suggests questions to discuss with a clinician.

output_examples.input: Review this wellness plan for safety language.
output: The response separates general wellness suggestions from medical claims.
It flags statements that could imply diagnosis or treatment.
It adds a reminder to seek qualified medical advice.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare for a non-urgent health appointment.
output: The response creates a concise visit summary.
It organizes symptoms, timeline, medicines, and questions.

best_practices: Use plain symptom descriptions with dates, duration, and severity when available.
Ask for general information and preparation support, not diagnosis or treatment decisions.
Review generated guidance with a qualified clinician for medical decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for emergencies or urgent symptoms.
Do not enter sensitive health data unless your AI tool and workspace are approved for it.
Do not present generated wellness guidance as a confirmed medical opinion.

faq.question: Does this skill diagnose conditions?
faq.answer: No. It supports organization and general information. A qualified clinician should make medical decisions.

faq.question: Can it track symptoms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help structure symptoms, dates, severity, and questions for follow-up.

faq.question: Does it store health records?
faq.answer: No evidence found in SKILL.md that it stores data or provides integrations.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it safe for emergencies?
faq.answer: No. Emergency symptoms require local emergency services or urgent clinical care.

faq.question: Why are network findings listed?
faq.answer: Static analysis detected GitHub links. They are reference links, not executable network behavior.
